storm.summary_layperson: No thunderstorm risk in the picture for Riverside this evening — expect a quiet, mostly cloudy stretch with steady breeze and nothing threatening on radar.
storm.local_effect_blurb: There's no storm to test the Sound's cooling effect tonight, and that buffer is thin anyway — the air-water gap is already down to under 5°F this afternoon and goes negative (water warmer than air) by around 7 PM.
storm.detail_html:
Radar out of KOKX shows no storm cells anywhere near Riverside this evening, and today's HRRR run puts CAPE at just 230 J/kg — very little instability to work with. The latest Area Forecast Discussion from OKX agrees, noting plainly that "instability overall appears to be lacking." There are no watches, warnings, or advisories in effect.

0-6km shear is a healthy 33.8 kt out of the WNW, but shear alone doesn't build storms — without instability there's nothing for it to organize. This is a shear-rich, CAPE-starved atmosphere, which is a low-risk combination for the cove and the wider region alike.

Because no storm is approaching, the Sound's usual protective marine-layer effect isn't being called on tonight. For the record, that layer is thin regardless: the air-water temperature gap is only 4.7°F now (Sound at 74°F, air at 79°F), and the trend data shows it falling below zero — water warmer than the cooling evening air — by around 7 PM. So even if something did try to develop later in the window, there would be no meaningful buffer left to lean on.

Bottom line: a calm, quiet evening for the cove and surrounding towns alike, with essentially no thunderstorm risk. The call would change only if a fresh line of convection appears upstream on radar, which nothing in the current data suggests.

wind.tactics_blurb: Moderate gradient wind with no sea breeze in play — steady S/SSW breeze in the 7-11 kt range holding right through sunset and beyond. Pressure is fairly even across the course; start mid-line and don't overcommit to one side.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This is a gradient-wind evening, not a sea-breeze day. The air-water temperature difference sits at 4.7°F, just under the 5°F thermal gate, and the sea-breeze ensemble isn't showing a real thermal signal — so the wind you feel tonight is straight synoptic flow, not a Sound-driven thermal.

The authoritative airport-anemometer average is 9.7 kt, squarely in the moderate-gradient band (8-15 kt). Direction is a clean, steady due south (~170-185°) all evening — HRRR and the western-LIS station ensemble agree closely (Riverside YC at 175°, HRRR forecasting 176-181° through the window), so there's no meaningful model/observation divergence to flag tonight.

Favored side: center. Due-south flow is the cleanest direction for this cove — it runs straight up the N-S axis with the most even pressure of any wind angle, so there's no strong geographic bias toward either shore. Expect steady direction with normal gust/lull cycling rather than organized oscillations.

Per the gradient-wind rule, this holds through sunset (7:13 PM) and beyond — no collapse expected. HRRR's usable forecast data runs out at 7:00 PM this cycle; the 8, 9, and 10 PM rows are extrapolated from the regime's normal behavior (1-2 kt of softening from nocturnal boundary-layer stabilization, not a dying trend). Expect 7-11 kt through the window — solidly in the sweet spot for one-design dinghies, easing toward the lower end of that range late. No postponement risk.
